wrong: He do not understand the question.
correct: He does not understand the question.
explanation_hi: 'He' के साथ 'does' का प्रयोग होता है।
explanation_en: Use 'does' with singular subjects.

wrong: She have two sisters.
correct: She has two sisters.
explanation_hi: Singular subject के साथ 'has' प्रयोग होता है।
explanation_en: Use 'has' with singular subjects.

wrong: They was playing football.
correct: They were playing football.
explanation_hi: 'They' के साथ 'were' प्रयोग होता है।
explanation_en: Use 'were' with plural subjects.

wrong: I am agree with you.
correct: I agree with you.
explanation_hi: 'Agree' adjective नहीं है; helping verb के साथ नहीं आता।
explanation_en: 'Agree' is a verb and does not take 'am' before it.

wrong: He returned back yesterday.
correct: He returned yesterday.
explanation_hi: 'Return' में वापस आने का अर्थ पहले से होता है।
explanation_en: 'Return' already means 'come back'; 'back' is redundant.

wrong: Discuss about the topic.
correct: Discuss the topic.
explanation_hi: 'Discuss' के बाद 'about' नहीं आता।
explanation_en: 'Discuss' is a transitive verb; do not use 'about' after it.

wrong: One of the boys are absent.
correct: One of the boys is absent.
explanation_hi: 'One' singular subject है।
explanation_en: The subject is 'one', which is singular; use 'is'.

wrong: Each boys got a prize.
correct: Each boy got a prize.
explanation_hi: 'Each' के बाद singular noun आता है।
explanation_en: 'Each' is followed by a singular noun.

wrong: He is senior than me.
correct: He is senior to me.
explanation_hi: Latin-rooted comparatives (senior, junior, superior, inferior, prior) के साथ 'to' प्रयोग होता है।
explanation_en: Latin-origin comparatives (senior, junior, superior, inferior) take 'to', not 'than'.

wrong: She is married with a doctor.
correct: She is married to a doctor.
explanation_hi: 'Married' के साथ 'to' आता है।
explanation_en: Use 'to' after 'married'.

wrong: I prefer tea than coffee.
correct: I prefer tea to coffee.
explanation_hi: 'Prefer' के साथ 'to' आता है, 'than' नहीं।
explanation_en: 'Prefer' takes 'to', not 'than', in comparison.

wrong: He is good in English.
correct: He is good at English.
explanation_hi: Skills/subjects के लिए 'good at' प्रयोग होता है।
explanation_en: Use 'good at' for skills and subjects.

wrong: She is suffering with fever.
correct: She is suffering from fever.
explanation_hi: 'Suffer' के साथ 'from' प्रयोग होता है।
explanation_en: Use 'from' after 'suffer'.

wrong: The sceneries are beautiful.
correct: The scenery is beautiful.
explanation_hi: 'Scenery' uncountable noun है; इसका plural नहीं बनता।
explanation_en: 'Scenery' is an uncountable noun and has no plural form.

wrong: Informations are useful.
correct: Information is useful.
explanation_hi: 'Information' uncountable noun है।
explanation_en: 'Information' is uncountable and does not take a plural form.

wrong: He gave me many advices.
correct: He gave me much advice.
explanation_hi: 'Advice' uncountable noun है।
explanation_en: 'Advice' is uncountable; use 'much' not 'many'.

wrong: She did not wrote the letter.
correct: She did not write the letter.
explanation_hi: 'Did' के बाद verb की first form (base form) आती है।
explanation_en: Use the base form of the verb after 'did'.

wrong: I am having a car.
correct: I have a car.
explanation_hi: Possession दिखाने के लिए 'have' continuous form में नहीं आता।
explanation_en: Stative verbs like 'have' (possession) are not used in continuous tense.

wrong: Neither Ram nor his friends was present.
correct: Neither Ram nor his friends were present.
explanation_hi: Verb nearest subject (friends) के अनुसार आता है।
explanation_en: With 'neither...nor', the verb agrees with the subject nearest to it.

wrong: Either of the books are useful.
correct: Either of the books is useful.
explanation_hi: 'Either of' के साथ singular verb आता है।
explanation_en: 'Either of' takes a singular verb.

wrong: He is one of those students who works hard.
correct: He is one of those students who work hard.
explanation_hi: Relative clause 'students' (plural) के अनुसार है।
explanation_en: The relative clause verb agrees with 'students', not 'one'.

wrong: She enjoys to dance.
correct: She enjoys dancing.
explanation_hi: 'Enjoy' के बाद gerund (-ing form) आता है।
explanation_en: 'Enjoy' is followed by a gerund, not an infinitive.

wrong: I look forward to meet you.
correct: I look forward to meeting you.
explanation_hi: 'Look forward to' में 'to' preposition है; इसके बाद gerund आता है।
explanation_en: 'To' in 'look forward to' is a preposition; use gerund after it.

wrong: No sooner he arrived than it started raining.
correct: No sooner had he arrived than it started raining.
explanation_hi: 'No sooner' के बाद subject-auxiliary inversion होता है।
explanation_en: Use subject-auxiliary inversion after 'No sooner'.

wrong: Hardly I had reached when he left.
correct: Hardly had I reached when he left.
explanation_hi: 'Hardly' sentence की शुरुआत में आने पर inversion होता है।
explanation_en: Use inversion (auxiliary before subject) when 'Hardly' starts a sentence.

wrong: He is accustomed with hard work.
correct: He is accustomed to hard work.
explanation_hi: 'Accustomed' के साथ 'to' प्रयोग होता है।
explanation_en: Use 'to' after 'accustomed'.

wrong: My father is angry on me.
correct: My father is angry with me.
explanation_hi: व्यक्ति के साथ 'angry with' प्रयोग होता है।
explanation_en: Use 'angry with' when referring to a person.

wrong: He insisted to go there.
correct: He insisted on going there.
explanation_hi: 'Insist' के साथ 'on + gerund' आता है।
explanation_en: Use 'on + gerund' after 'insist'.

wrong: He is taller than any boy in the class.
correct: He is taller than any other boy in the class.
explanation_hi: Same group comparison में 'any other' प्रयोग होता है।
explanation_en: Use 'any other' when comparing within the same group.

wrong: This is more better.
correct: This is better.
explanation_hi: 'Better' already comparative है; 'more' जोड़ना double comparative है।
explanation_en: 'Better' is already comparative; do not use 'more better'.

wrong: He is the most smartest boy.
correct: He is the smartest boy.
explanation_hi: 'Smartest' already superlative है; 'most' जोड़ना double superlative है।
explanation_en: 'Smartest' is already superlative; do not add 'most'.

wrong: She is my cousin sister.
correct: She is my cousin.
explanation_hi: 'Cousin' gender-neutral होता है; 'sister' जोड़ना अनावश्यक है।
explanation_en: 'Cousin' is gender-neutral; adding 'sister' or 'brother' is incorrect.

wrong: Myself Rahul.
correct: I am Rahul.
explanation_hi: Reflexive pronoun 'myself' self-introduction के लिए प्रयोग नहीं होता।
explanation_en: Do not use 'myself' to introduce yourself; use 'I am'.

wrong: He denied to help me.
correct: He denied helping me.
explanation_hi: 'Deny' के बाद gerund आता है।
explanation_en: Use gerund after 'deny'.

wrong: She prevented me to go there.
correct: She prevented me from going there.
explanation_hi: 'Prevent someone from + gerund' सही structure है।
explanation_en: Use 'from + gerund' after 'prevent'.

wrong: He ordered for tea.
correct: He ordered tea.
explanation_hi: 'Order' transitive verb है; 'for' आवश्यक नहीं।
explanation_en: 'Order' is transitive; do not add 'for' before the object.

wrong: The police is investigating the case.
correct: The police are investigating the case.
explanation_hi: 'Police' collective noun है जो plural verb लेता है।
explanation_en: 'Police' is treated as a plural noun and takes a plural verb.

wrong: Mathematics are difficult.
correct: Mathematics is difficult.
explanation_hi: '-ics' subjects (Mathematics, Physics, Economics) singular verb लेते हैं।
explanation_en: Subjects ending in '-ics' take singular verbs.

wrong: The news are true.
correct: The news is true.
explanation_hi: 'News' singular uncountable noun है।
explanation_en: 'News' is a singular uncountable noun; use singular verb.

wrong: He is addicted with drugs.
correct: He is addicted to drugs.
explanation_hi: 'Addicted' के साथ 'to' प्रयोग होता है।
explanation_en: Use 'to' after 'addicted'.

wrong: She resembles with her mother.
correct: She resembles her mother.
explanation_hi: 'Resemble' transitive verb है; preposition नहीं आता।
explanation_en: 'Resemble' is transitive; do not use a preposition after it.

wrong: He entered into the room.
correct: He entered the room.
explanation_hi: 'Enter' transitive verb है; 'into' नहीं आता।
explanation_en: 'Enter' is transitive; do not use 'into' after it.

wrong: He lacks of confidence.
correct: He lacks confidence.
explanation_hi: 'Lack' (verb) के साथ 'of' नहीं आता।
explanation_en: Do not use 'of' after 'lack' when used as a verb.

wrong: I cannot cope up with pressure.
correct: I cannot cope with pressure.
explanation_hi: 'Cope with' सही phrase है; 'up' अनावश्यक है।
explanation_en: The correct phrase is 'cope with'; do not add 'up'.

wrong: She emphasized on discipline.
correct: She emphasized discipline.
explanation_hi: 'Emphasize' transitive verb है; 'on' नहीं आता।
explanation_en: 'Emphasize' is transitive; do not use 'on' after it.

wrong: The meeting will be held on tomorrow.
correct: The meeting will be held tomorrow.
explanation_hi: 'Tomorrow' adverb है; इससे पहले preposition नहीं आता।
explanation_en: 'Tomorrow' is an adverb; do not use a preposition before it.

wrong: He is capable to do this work.
correct: He is capable of doing this work.
explanation_hi: 'Capable' के साथ 'of + gerund' आता है।
explanation_en: Use 'of + gerund' after 'capable'.

wrong: He is addicted in gambling.
correct: He is addicted to gambling.
explanation_hi: 'Addicted to' सही phrase है।
explanation_en: Use 'to' after 'addicted'.

wrong: The man is devoid from fear.
correct: The man is devoid of fear.
explanation_hi: 'Devoid of' सही phrase है।
explanation_en: Use 'of' after 'devoid'.

wrong: He is different than me.
correct: He is different from me.
explanation_hi: 'Different from' सही phrase है।
explanation_en: Use 'from' after 'different'.

wrong: He is eligible for appear in the exam.
correct: He is eligible to appear in the exam.
explanation_hi: 'Eligible to + infinitive' सही structure है।
explanation_en: Use infinitive after 'eligible'.

wrong: She is fond for music.
correct: She is fond of music.
explanation_hi: 'Fond of' सही phrase है।
explanation_en: Use 'of' after 'fond'.

wrong: He was guilty for theft.
correct: He was guilty of theft.
explanation_hi: 'Guilty of' सही phrase है।
explanation_en: Use 'of' after 'guilty'.

wrong: I am hopeful to success.
correct: I am hopeful of success.
explanation_hi: 'Hopeful of' सही phrase है।
explanation_en: Use 'of' after 'hopeful'.

wrong: He is junior than me.
correct: He is junior to me.
explanation_hi: Latin-origin comparatives 'to' लेते हैं।
explanation_en: Latin-origin comparatives take 'to', not 'than'.

wrong: She is lacking of confidence.
correct: She lacks confidence.
explanation_hi: 'Lack' verb के साथ 'of' नहीं आता।
explanation_en: Use 'lack' directly without 'of'.

wrong: He ordered me for leave the room.
correct: He ordered me to leave the room.
explanation_hi: 'Order someone to + infinitive' सही structure है।
explanation_en: Use infinitive after 'order someone'.

wrong: She resembles to her sister.
correct: She resembles her sister.
explanation_hi: 'Resemble' के बाद preposition नहीं आता।
explanation_en: Do not use preposition after 'resemble'.

wrong: He was surprised on my behavior.
correct: He was surprised at my behavior.
explanation_hi: 'Surprised at' सही phrase है।
explanation_en: Use 'at' after 'surprised'.

wrong: She is tired from work.
correct: She is tired of work.
explanation_hi: 'Tired of' सही phrase है।
explanation_en: Use 'of' after 'tired'.

wrong: He was vexed on me.
correct: He was vexed with me.
explanation_hi: 'Vexed with' सही phrase है।
explanation_en: Use 'with' after 'vexed'.

wrong: The room was infected by mosquitoes.
correct: The room was infested with mosquitoes.
explanation_hi: कीड़े-मकोड़ों के लिए 'infested with' प्रयोग होता है।
explanation_en: Use 'infested with' for insects or pests; 'infected' means diseased.

wrong: The teacher is popular between students.
correct: The teacher is popular among students.
explanation_hi: दो से अधिक लोगों के बीच 'among' प्रयोग होता है।
explanation_en: Use 'among' for more than two people.

wrong: Distribute the sweets between the students.
correct: Distribute the sweets among the students.
explanation_hi: अनेक लोगों के बीच 'among' प्रयोग होता है।
explanation_en: Use 'among' when distributing to more than two.

wrong: One should keep his promise.
correct: One should keep one's promise.
explanation_hi: 'One' के साथ 'one's' pronoun प्रयोग होता है।
explanation_en: Use 'one's' as the pronoun for 'one'.

wrong: None of the information are useful.
correct: None of the information is useful.
explanation_hi: 'Information' uncountable noun है; singular verb आता है।
explanation_en: 'Information' is uncountable; use singular verb.

wrong: Physics are my favorite subject.
correct: Physics is my favorite subject.
explanation_hi: '-ics' subjects singular verb लेते हैं।
explanation_en: Subjects ending in '-ics' take singular verbs.

wrong: The cattle is grazing.
correct: The cattle are grazing.
explanation_hi: 'Cattle' हमेशा plural होता है।
explanation_en: 'Cattle' is always plural and takes a plural verb.

wrong: People is happy with the result.
correct: People are happy with the result.
explanation_hi: 'People' plural noun है।
explanation_en: 'People' is plural and takes a plural verb.

wrong: A pair of shoes are lying there.
correct: A pair of shoes is lying there.
explanation_hi: 'A pair of' singular unit है; singular verb आता है।
explanation_en: 'A pair of' is singular; use a singular verb.

wrong: The committee are divided in its opinion.
correct: The committee is divided in its opinion.
explanation_hi: एक इकाई के रूप में collective noun singular verb लेता है।
explanation_en: When acting as a unit, a collective noun takes a singular verb.

wrong: Scarcely had I reached than the train left.
correct: Scarcely had I reached when the train left.
explanation_hi: 'Scarcely' के साथ 'when' आता है, 'than' नहीं।
explanation_en: Use 'when' (not 'than') with 'scarcely'.

wrong: No sooner did he see me when he ran away.
correct: No sooner did he see me than he ran away.
explanation_hi: 'No sooner' के साथ 'than' आता है।
explanation_en: Use 'than' (not 'when') with 'no sooner'.

wrong: Hardly he had entered when it rained.
correct: Hardly had he entered when it rained.
explanation_hi: 'Hardly' sentence शुरू में आने पर inversion होता है।
explanation_en: Use inversion after 'Hardly' at the start of a sentence.

wrong: He asked me that why I was late.
correct: He asked me why I was late.
explanation_hi: Indirect question में 'that' नहीं आता।
explanation_en: Do not use 'that' to introduce indirect questions.

wrong: The teacher asked to me a question.
correct: The teacher asked me a question.
explanation_hi: 'Ask' के साथ object सीधे आता है।
explanation_en: Do not use 'to' before the indirect object after 'ask'.

wrong: He explained me the rule.
correct: He explained the rule to me.
explanation_hi: 'Explain something to someone' सही structure है।
explanation_en: Use 'explain something to someone'; not 'explain someone something'.

wrong: She described me the scene.
correct: She described the scene to me.
explanation_hi: 'Describe something to someone' सही structure है।
explanation_en: Use 'describe something to someone'.

wrong: I suggested him to leave.
correct: I suggested that he leave.
explanation_hi: 'Suggest' के बाद clause आता है, infinitive नहीं।
explanation_en: Use a 'that-clause' after 'suggest', not an infinitive.

wrong: He is too clever to not understand this.
correct: He is too clever not to understand this.
explanation_hi: 'Too...not to' structure में 'not' infinitive के पहले आता है।
explanation_en: In 'too...to' structure, 'not' comes before the infinitive.

wrong: She has no any friends.
correct: She has no friends.
explanation_hi: 'No' और 'any' एक साथ नहीं आते।
explanation_en: Do not use 'no' and 'any' together; it creates a double negative.

wrong: I don't know nothing.
correct: I don't know anything.
explanation_hi: Double negative (don't + nothing) गलत है।
explanation_en: Avoid double negatives; use 'anything' with 'don't'.

wrong: He seldom or ever goes there.
correct: He seldom or never goes there.
explanation_hi: 'Seldom or never' सही idiomatic expression है।
explanation_en: The correct expression is 'seldom or never', not 'seldom or ever'.

wrong: The boy was punished of theft.
correct: The boy was punished for theft.
explanation_hi: 'Punished for' सही phrase है।
explanation_en: Use 'for' after 'punished'.

wrong: He died with cancer.
correct: He died of cancer.
explanation_hi: Disease/illness से मृत्यु के लिए 'die of' प्रयोग होता है।
explanation_en: Use 'die of' when the cause of death is a disease.

wrong: The child is crying from hunger.
correct: The child is crying with hunger.
explanation_hi: Emotion/condition के लिए 'with' प्रयोग होता है।
explanation_en: Use 'with' to express the emotion or condition causing the action.

wrong: He is angry upon me.
correct: He is angry with me.
explanation_hi: व्यक्ति के साथ 'angry with' प्रयोग होता है।
explanation_en: Use 'angry with' when referring to a person.

wrong: He congratulated me for my success.
correct: He congratulated me on my success.
explanation_hi: 'Congratulate someone on something' सही structure है।
explanation_en: Use 'on' after 'congratulate'.

wrong: She is capable to solve the problem.
correct: She is capable of solving the problem.
explanation_hi: 'Capable of + gerund' सही structure है।
explanation_en: Use 'of + gerund' after 'capable'.

wrong: He prevented me to enter the room.
correct: He prevented me from entering the room.
explanation_hi: 'Prevent someone from + gerund' सही structure है।
explanation_en: Use 'from + gerund' after 'prevent'.

wrong: I objected his proposal.
correct: I objected to his proposal.
explanation_hi: 'Object to' सही phrase है।
explanation_en: Use 'to' after 'object'.

wrong: She is devoted for her family.
correct: She is devoted to her family.
explanation_hi: 'Devoted to' सही phrase है।
explanation_en: Use 'to' after 'devoted'.

wrong: He has applied for the post yesterday.
correct: He applied for the post yesterday.
explanation_hi: Definite past time ('yesterday') के साथ simple past आता है।
explanation_en: Use simple past (not present perfect) with definite past time expressions.

wrong: I am here since Monday.
correct: I have been here since Monday.
explanation_hi: 'Since' के साथ present perfect tense प्रयोग होता है।
explanation_en: Use present perfect tense with 'since'.

wrong: He is married with her since 2010.
correct: He has been married to her since 2010.
explanation_hi: 'Married to' और 'since' के साथ perfect tense प्रयोग होता है।
explanation_en: Use 'married to' and present perfect tense with 'since'.

wrong: I did not knew the answer.
correct: I did not know the answer.
explanation_hi: 'Did' के बाद verb की base form आती है।
explanation_en: Use the base form of the verb after 'did'.

wrong: She is knowing him very well.
correct: She knows him very well.
explanation_hi: 'Know' stative verb है; continuous tense में नहीं आता।
explanation_en: Stative verbs like 'know' are not used in continuous tense.

wrong: He has much friends here.
correct: He has many friends here.
explanation_hi: Countable noun के साथ 'many' प्रयोग होता है।
explanation_en: Use 'many' with countable nouns; 'much' is for uncountable nouns.

wrong: There are less students in the class.
correct: There are fewer students in the class.
explanation_hi: Countable noun के लिए 'fewer' प्रयोग होता है।
explanation_en: Use 'fewer' with countable nouns; 'less' is for uncountable nouns.

wrong: The meeting was comprised of five members.
correct: The meeting comprised five members.
explanation_hi: 'Comprise' active form में प्रयोग होता है; 'of' नहीं आता।
explanation_en: 'Comprise' is used in active voice and does not take 'of'.

wrong: The match was postponed due to rain heavily.
correct: The match was postponed due to heavy rain.
explanation_hi: Adjective noun के पहले आता है।
explanation_en: Use adjective before noun; 'heavy rain', not 'rain heavily'.

wrong: He denied to have stolen the money.
correct: He denied having stolen the money.
explanation_hi: 'Deny' के बाद gerund आता है।
explanation_en: Use gerund after 'deny'.

wrong: She is too weak so that she cannot walk.
correct: She is so weak that she cannot walk.
explanation_hi: 'So...that' सही structure है।
explanation_en: Use 'so...that' structure; not 'too...so that'.

wrong: I could not help but to laugh.
correct: I could not help but laugh.
explanation_hi: 'Cannot help but' के बाद base verb आता है।
explanation_en: Use bare infinitive (base form) after 'cannot help but'.

wrong: He hardly never comes late.
correct: He hardly ever comes late.
explanation_hi: 'Hardly' negative है; 'never' जोड़ना double negative है।
explanation_en: 'Hardly' is itself negative; do not use 'never' with it.

wrong: No less than ten persons was injured.
correct: No less than ten persons were injured.
explanation_hi: Plural noun 'persons' के साथ plural verb आता है।
explanation_en: Use plural verb with plural noun 'persons'.

wrong: The principal along with teachers were present.
correct: The principal along with teachers was present.
explanation_hi: 'Along with' के साथ verb पहले subject के अनुसार आता है।
explanation_en: When 'along with' connects subjects, the verb agrees with the first subject.

wrong: I have been waiting you for two hours.
correct: I have been waiting for you for two hours.
explanation_hi: 'Wait for' सही phrase है।
explanation_en: Use 'for' before the object with 'wait'.

wrong: He ordered that the work should be completed immediately.
correct: He ordered that the work be completed immediately.
explanation_hi: 'Order' के बाद subjunctive form प्रयोग होता है।
explanation_en: Use subjunctive (base form) in 'that-clause' after 'order'.

wrong: If I was you, I would refuse.
correct: If I were you, I would refuse.
explanation_hi: Unreal/hypothetical condition में 'were' प्रयोग होता है।
explanation_en: Use 'were' (not 'was') in unreal or hypothetical conditions.

wrong: I wish I was rich.
correct: I wish I were rich.
explanation_hi: 'Wish' के साथ unreal condition में 'were' प्रयोग होता है।
explanation_en: Use 'were' after 'wish' for unreal situations.

wrong: He talks as if he is mad.
correct: He talks as if he were mad.
explanation_hi: 'As if' के साथ unreal condition में 'were' प्रयोग होता है।
explanation_en: Use 'were' after 'as if' for imaginary conditions.

wrong: She is one of the girls who sings well.
correct: She is one of the girls who sing well.
explanation_hi: Relative clause plural noun 'girls' के अनुसार है।

explanation_hi: Proposal के लिए 'agree to' और 'last night' सही है।
explanation_en: Use 'agree to' for proposals; use 'last night', not 'yesterday night'.

wrong: The officer appealed the people for calm.
correct: The officer appealed to the people for calm.
explanation_hi: 'Appeal to someone for something' सही structure है।
explanation_en: Use 'to' after 'appeal'.

wrong: The doctor attended the patient carefully.
correct: The doctor attended to the patient carefully.
explanation_hi: 'Attend to' सही phrase है।
explanation_en: Use 'to' after 'attend'.

wrong: The teacher blamed me of carelessness.
correct: The teacher blamed me for carelessness.
explanation_hi: 'Blame someone for something' सही structure है।
explanation_en: Use 'for' after 'blame'.

wrong: The teacher cautioned me for the danger.
correct: The teacher cautioned me against the danger.
explanation_hi: 'Caution someone against something' सही structure है।
explanation_en: Use 'against' after 'caution'.

wrong: The officer charged him of theft.
correct: The officer charged him with theft.
explanation_hi: 'Charge someone with something' सही structure है।
explanation_en: Use 'with' after 'charge'.

wrong: The teacher commented the issue openly.
correct: The teacher commented on the issue openly.
explanation_hi: 'Comment on' सही phrase है।
explanation_en: Use 'on' after 'comment'.

wrong: The officer communicated me the decision.
correct: The officer communicated the decision to me.
explanation_hi: 'Communicate something to someone' सही structure है।
explanation_en: Use 'communicate something to someone'.

wrong: The child complained against headache.
correct: The child complained of headache.
explanation_hi: Illness/pain के लिए 'complain of' प्रयोग होता है।
explanation_en: Use 'of' for illness after 'complain'.

wrong: The manager complied my request quickly.
correct: The manager complied with my request quickly.
explanation_hi: 'Comply with' सही phrase है।
explanation_en: Use 'with' after 'comply'.

wrong: The students confided each other their secrets.
correct: The students confided their secrets to each other.
explanation_hi: 'Confide something to someone' सही structure है।
explanation_en: Use 'confide something to someone'.

wrong: The teacher convinced me for his honesty.
correct: The teacher convinced me of his honesty.
explanation_hi: 'Convince someone of something' सही structure है।
explanation_en: Use 'of' after 'convince'.

wrong: The officer dealt the matter wisely.
correct: The officer dealt with the matter wisely.
explanation_hi: 'Deal with' सही phrase है।
explanation_en: Use 'with' after 'deal'.

wrong: The child died from hunger.
correct: The child died of hunger.
explanation_hi: 'Die of' disease/hunger के लिए प्रयोग होता है।
explanation_en: Use 'die of' for disease or deprivation.

wrong: The officer differed with my opinion completely.
correct: The officer differed from my opinion completely.
explanation_hi: 'Differ from' सही phrase है।
explanation_en: Use 'from' after 'differ'.

wrong: The teacher disposed all useless papers.
correct: The teacher disposed of all useless papers.
explanation_hi: 'Dispose of' सही phrase है।
explanation_en: Use 'of' after 'dispose'.

wrong: The officer excused me from attending the meeting.
correct: The officer excused me for not attending the meeting.
explanation_hi: 'Excuse someone for something' सही structure है।
explanation_en: Use 'excuse for' appropriately.

wrong: The teacher favoured to my proposal.
correct: The teacher favoured my proposal.
explanation_hi: 'Favour' transitive verb है; preposition नहीं आता।
explanation_en: 'Favour' is transitive; do not use a preposition after it.

wrong: The officer furnished all information to us.
correct: The officer furnished us with all information.
explanation_hi: 'Furnish someone with something' सही structure है।
explanation_en: Use 'furnish someone with something'.

wrong: The teacher informed me the schedule yesterday.
correct: The teacher informed me of the schedule yesterday.
explanation_hi: 'Inform someone of something' सही structure है।
explanation_en: Use 'inform someone of something'.

wrong: The officer insisted for immediate action.
correct: The officer insisted on immediate action.
explanation_hi: 'Insist on' सही phrase है।
explanation_en: Use 'on' after 'insist'.

wrong: The manager interfered on my work unnecessarily.
correct: The manager interfered with my work unnecessarily.
explanation_hi: 'Interfere with' सही phrase है।
explanation_en: Use 'with' after 'interfere'.

wrong: The officer laughed upon my mistake.
correct: The officer laughed at my mistake.
explanation_hi: 'Laugh at' सही phrase है।
explanation_en: Use 'at' after 'laugh'.

wrong: The teacher objected the proposal strongly.
correct: The teacher objected to the proposal strongly.
explanation_hi: 'Object to' सही phrase है।
explanation_en: Use 'to' after 'object'.

wrong: The child obeyed to his parents always.
correct: The child obeyed his parents always.
explanation_hi: 'Obey' transitive verb है; preposition नहीं आता।
explanation_en: 'Obey' is transitive; do not use a preposition after it.

wrong: The teacher pointed towards the blackboard clearly.
correct: The teacher pointed at the blackboard clearly.
explanation_hi: 'Point at' (किसी वस्तु की ओर इशारा) सही phrase है।
explanation_en: Use 'point at' when indicating something.

wrong: The officer replied my question immediately.
correct: The officer replied to my question immediately.
explanation_hi: 'Reply to' सही phrase है।
explanation_en: Use 'to' after 'reply'.

wrong: The teacher requested me to not make noise.
correct: The teacher requested me not to make noise.
explanation_hi: 'Not' को infinitive से पहले रखा जाता है।
explanation_en: Place 'not' before the infinitive.

wrong: The officer searched the missing file everywhere.
correct: The officer searched for the missing file everywhere.
explanation_hi: 'Search for' सही phrase है।
explanation_en: Use 'for' after 'search'.

wrong: The officer suspected on his intentions.
correct: The officer suspected his intentions.
explanation_hi: 'Suspect' transitive verb है; 'on' नहीं आता।
explanation_en: 'Suspect' is transitive; do not use 'on' after it.

wrong: The teacher thanked me for helping him very much.
correct: The teacher thanked me very much for helping him.
explanation_hi: Adverb 'very much' verb के बाद आता है।
explanation_en: Place adverb 'very much' after the verb, not at the end.

wrong: The child trembled by fear during the storm.
correct: The child trembled with fear during the storm.
explanation_hi: 'Tremble with fear' सही phrase है।
explanation_en: Use 'with fear'.

wrong: The officer warned me against to enter the room.
correct: The officer warned me against entering the room.
explanation_hi: 'Against' के बाद gerund आता है।
explanation_en: Use gerund after 'against'.

wrong: The officer yielded before public pressure.
correct: The officer yielded to public pressure.
explanation_hi: 'Yield to' सही phrase है।
explanation_en: Use 'to' after 'yield'.

wrong: The boy is weak in English but good in Mathematics.
correct: The boy is weak in English but good at Mathematics.
explanation_hi: Skills/subjects की mastery के लिए 'good at' प्रयोग होता है।
explanation_en: Use 'good at' for skills or subjects; 'weak in' is correct as given.

wrong: He is superior than me in intelligence.
correct: He is superior to me in intelligence.
explanation_hi: Latin-origin comparatives 'to' लेते हैं।
explanation_en: Latin-origin comparatives take 'to', not 'than'.

wrong: This pen is preferable than that one.
correct: This pen is preferable to that one.
explanation_hi: 'Preferable to' सही phrase है।
explanation_en: Use 'to' after 'preferable'.

wrong: The train is preferable than the bus.
correct: The train is preferable to the bus.
explanation_hi: 'Preferable to' सही phrase है।
explanation_en: Use 'to' after 'preferable'.

wrong: He is equal than me in strength.
correct: He is equal to me in strength.
explanation_hi: 'Equal to' सही phrase है।
explanation_en: Use 'to' after 'equal'.

wrong: She is related with my uncle.
correct: She is related to my uncle.
explanation_hi: 'Related to' सही phrase है।
explanation_en: Use 'to' after 'related'.

wrong: He is acquainted to the principal.
correct: He is acquainted with the principal.
explanation_hi: 'Acquainted with' सही phrase है।
explanation_en: Use 'with' after 'acquainted'.

wrong: The teacher is pleased from your performance.
correct: The teacher is pleased with your performance.
explanation_hi: 'Pleased with' सही phrase है।
explanation_en: Use 'with' after 'pleased'.

wrong: The officer is satisfied from the report.
correct: The officer is satisfied with the report.
explanation_hi: 'Satisfied with' सही phrase है।
explanation_en: Use 'with' after 'satisfied'.

wrong: He is annoyed from the noise.
correct: He is annoyed with the noise.
explanation_hi: 'Annoyed with' सही phrase है।
explanation_en: Use 'with' after 'annoyed'.

wrong: She is disgusted from his behavior.
correct: She is disgusted with his behavior.
explanation_hi: 'Disgusted with' सही phrase है।
explanation_en: Use 'with' after 'disgusted'.

wrong: He is expert in repairing machines.
correct: He is expert at repairing machines.
explanation_hi: Skill के लिए 'expert at' प्रयोग होता है।
explanation_en: Use 'at' for expertise in a skill.

wrong: He is devoid from sympathy.
correct: He is devoid of sympathy.
explanation_hi: 'Devoid of' सही phrase है।
explanation_en: Use 'of' after 'devoid'.

wrong: She is bent to become a doctor.
correct: She is bent on becoming a doctor.
explanation_hi: 'Bent on + gerund' सही structure है।
explanation_en: Use 'on + gerund' after 'bent'.

wrong: The child is incapable to solve the puzzle.
correct: The child is incapable of solving the puzzle.
explanation_hi: 'Incapable of + gerund' सही structure है।
explanation_en: Use 'of + gerund' after 'incapable'.

wrong: He is confident to win the election.
correct: He is confident of winning the election.
explanation_hi: 'Confident of + gerund' सही structure है।
explanation_en: Use 'of + gerund' after 'confident'.

wrong: The officer is desirous to meet the minister.
correct: The officer is desirous of meeting the minister.
explanation_hi: 'Desirous of + gerund' सही structure है।
explanation_en: Use 'of + gerund' after 'desirous'.

wrong: The teacher is conscious for her duties.
correct: The teacher is conscious of her duties.
explanation_hi: 'Conscious of' सही phrase है।
explanation_en: Use 'of' after 'conscious'.

wrong: He is addicted with alcohol.
correct: He is addicted to alcohol.
explanation_hi: 'Addicted to' सही phrase है।
explanation_en: Use 'to' after 'addicted'.

wrong: The principal is opposed for the proposal.
correct: The principal is opposed to the proposal.
explanation_hi: 'Opposed to' सही phrase है।
explanation_en: Use 'to' after 'opposed'.

wrong: The officer is indebted with his friend.
correct: The officer is indebted to his friend.
explanation_hi: 'Indebted to' सही phrase है।
explanation_en: Use 'to' after 'indebted'.

wrong: He is fond for reading novels.
correct: He is fond of reading novels.
explanation_hi: 'Fond of' सही phrase है।
explanation_en: Use 'of' after 'fond'.

wrong: She is grateful for me for the help.
correct: She is grateful to me for the help.
explanation_hi: 'Grateful to someone for something' सही structure है।
explanation_en: Use 'grateful to someone for something'.

wrong: The officer is negligent from his duties.
correct: The officer is negligent of his duties.
explanation_hi: 'Negligent of' सही phrase है।
explanation_en: Use 'of' after 'negligent'.

wrong: The child is obedient with his parents.
correct: The child is obedient to his parents.
explanation_hi: 'Obedient to' सही phrase है।
explanation_en: Use 'to' after 'obedient'.

wrong: The teacher is partial for hardworking students.
correct: The teacher is partial to hardworking students.
explanation_hi: 'Partial to' सही phrase है।
explanation_en: Use 'to' after 'partial'.

wrong: The child is proficient for drawing.
correct: The child is proficient in drawing.
explanation_hi: 'Proficient in' सही phrase है।
explanation_en: Use 'in' after 'proficient'.

wrong: The teacher is proud for her students.
correct: The teacher is proud of her students.
explanation_hi: 'Proud of' सही phrase है।
explanation_en: Use 'of' after 'proud'.

wrong: The officer is responsible of the project.
correct: The officer is responsible for the project.
explanation_hi: 'Responsible for' सही phrase है।
explanation_en: Use 'for' after 'responsible'.

wrong: The child is sensitive for criticism.
correct: The child is sensitive to criticism.
explanation_hi: 'Sensitive to' सही phrase है।
explanation_en: Use 'to' after 'sensitive'.

wrong: The teacher is short from temper.
correct: The teacher is short-tempered.
explanation_hi: 'Short-tempered' एक compound adjective है।
explanation_en: Use the compound adjective 'short-tempered'.

wrong: The officer is worthy for praise.
correct: The officer is worthy of praise.
explanation_hi: 'Worthy of' सही phrase है।
explanation_en: Use 'of' after 'worthy'.

wrong: The teacher was absent since two days.
correct: The teacher has been absent for two days.
explanation_hi: Duration के लिए 'for' और perfect tense प्रयोग होता है।
explanation_en: Use 'for' with duration; use perfect tense.

wrong: The officer has been working here since five years.
correct: The officer has been working here for five years.
explanation_hi: Duration के लिए 'for' प्रयोग होता है।
explanation_en: Use 'for' (not 'since') with a period of time.

wrong: The child did not went to school yesterday.
correct: The child did not go to school yesterday.
explanation_hi: 'Did' के बाद verb की base form आती है।
explanation_en: Use the base form after 'did'.

wrong: The teacher had already saw the report.
correct: The teacher had already seen the report.
explanation_hi: Perfect tense में past participle (third form) प्रयोग होती है।
explanation_en: Use the past participle in perfect tense.

wrong: The officer has wrote the letter already.
correct: The officer has written the letter already.
explanation_hi: Perfect tense में past participle प्रयोग होती है।
explanation_en: Use the past participle in perfect tense.

wrong: The child is reading since morning.
correct: The child has been reading since morning.
explanation_hi: 'Since' के साथ present perfect continuous tense प्रयोग होता है।
explanation_en: Use present perfect continuous tense with 'since'.

wrong: The teacher has been teaching since ten years.
correct: The teacher has been teaching for ten years.
explanation_hi: Duration के लिए 'for' प्रयोग होता है।
explanation_en: Use 'for' with a duration of time.

wrong: The officer is having three cars.
correct: The officer has three cars.
explanation_hi: Possession के लिए continuous tense नहीं आता।
explanation_en: Do not use continuous tense for possession.

wrong: The child is knowing the answer correctly.
correct: The child knows the answer correctly.
explanation_hi: 'Know' stative verb है; continuous में नहीं आता।
explanation_en: Stative verbs like 'know' are not used in continuous tense.

wrong: The teacher is understanding your problem now.
correct: The teacher understands your problem now.
explanation_hi: 'Understand' stative verb है; continuous में नहीं आता।
explanation_en: Stative verbs like 'understand' are not used in continuous tense.

wrong: The officer has no any information regarding the case.
correct: The officer has no information regarding the case.
explanation_hi: 'No' और 'any' एक साथ नहीं आते।
explanation_en: Do not use 'no' and 'any' together.

wrong: The child does not know nothing about it.
correct: The child does not know anything about it.
explanation_hi: Double negative गलत है।
explanation_en: Avoid double negatives.

wrong: The teacher seldom never gets angry.
correct: The teacher seldom gets angry.
explanation_hi: 'Seldom' खुद negative है; 'never' जोड़ना double negative है।
explanation_en: 'Seldom' is already negative; do not add 'never'.

wrong: The officer returned back from Delhi yesterday.
correct: The officer returned from Delhi yesterday.
explanation_hi: 'Return' में वापस आने का अर्थ पहले से होता है।
explanation_en: 'Return' already implies coming back; 'back' is redundant.

wrong: The child repeated again the same mistake.
correct: The child repeated the same mistake.
explanation_hi: 'Repeat' में again का अर्थ पहले से होता है।
explanation_en: 'Repeat' already includes the idea of 'again'.

wrong: She is an university student.
correct: She is a university student.
explanation_hi: 'University' 'यू' (consonant sound) से शुरू होता है इसलिए 'a' आता है।
explanation_en: 'University' begins with a consonant sound /j/; use 'a', not 'an'.

wrong: He is a honest man.
correct: He is an honest man.
explanation_hi: 'Honest' में 'H' silent है; vowel sound से शुरू होने पर 'an' आता है।
explanation_en: 'Honest' begins with a silent 'H' and a vowel sound; use 'an'.

wrong: He is a heir to the throne.
correct: He is an heir to the throne.
explanation_hi: 'Heir' में 'H' silent है; vowel sound से शुरू होने पर 'an' आता है।
explanation_en: 'Heir' begins with a silent 'H' and vowel sound; use 'an'.

wrong: I saw a one-eyed man.
correct: I saw a one-eyed man.
explanation_hi: 'One' 'वन' (W sound, consonant) से शुरू होता है इसलिए 'a' सही है।
explanation_en: 'One' begins with a /w/ consonant sound; 'a' is correct.

wrong: He has an MA degree.
correct: He has an MA degree.
explanation_hi: Abbreviation में पहले letter का sound देखा जाता है; 'M' vowel sound /em/ देता है।
explanation_en: When reading abbreviations, check the first letter sound; 'M' sounds like /em/ (vowel sound).

wrong: He is the best student of a class.
correct: He is the best student of the class.
explanation_hi: Specific/particular noun के पहले 'the' आता है।
explanation_en: Use 'the' before a specific or particular noun.

wrong: Sun rises in east.
correct: The sun rises in the east.
explanation_hi: Unique objects (sun, moon) और directions के पहले 'the' आता है।
explanation_en: Use 'the' before unique objects like the sun and before directions.

wrong: She plays piano very well.
correct: She plays the piano very well.
explanation_hi: Musical instruments के पहले 'the' आता है।
explanation_en: Use 'the' before musical instruments.

wrong: He is in hospital.
correct: He is in the hospital.
explanation_hi: American English में hospital के पहले 'the' आता है।
explanation_en: Use 'the' before 'hospital' in standard usage.

wrong: Gold is a most valuable metal.
correct: Gold is the most valuable metal.
explanation_hi: Superlative degree के पहले 'the' आता है।
explanation_en: Use 'the' before superlatives.

wrong: I met a MP yesterday.
correct: I met an MP yesterday.
explanation_hi: Abbreviation 'MP' vowel sound /em/ से शुरू होता है।
explanation_en: Abbreviation 'MP' starts with vowel sound /em/; use 'an'.

wrong: He gave me an useful information.
correct: He gave me useful information.
explanation_hi: 'Useful' /j/ consonant sound से शुरू होता है; 'a useful' सही था, पर 'information' uncountable है।
explanation_en: 'Information' is uncountable; no article needed. 'Useful' takes 'a' (consonant sound /j/).

wrong: The wisdom is a virtue.
correct: Wisdom is a virtue.
explanation_hi: Abstract nouns general sense में article नहीं लेते।
explanation_en: Abstract nouns used in a general sense do not take an article.

wrong: The honesty is the best policy.
correct: Honesty is the best policy.
explanation_hi: Proverbs और general abstract nouns article नहीं लेते।
explanation_en: Abstract nouns in general or proverbial statements do not take an article.

wrong: He returned after the hour.
correct: He returned after an hour.
explanation_hi: 'Hour' silent 'H' से शुरू होता है; vowel sound के लिए 'an' आता है।
explanation_en: 'Hour' has a silent 'H' and begins with a vowel sound; use 'an'.

wrong: She is the teacher by profession.
correct: She is a teacher by profession.
explanation_hi: Profession बताते समय 'a/an' आता है।
explanation_en: When stating a profession, use 'a/an'.

wrong: He is best player in the team.
correct: He is the best player in the team.
explanation_hi: Superlative adjective के पहले 'the' आता है।
explanation_en: Use 'the' before a superlative adjective.

wrong: India is secular country.
correct: India is a secular country.
explanation_hi: Singular countable noun के पहले article आना चाहिए।
explanation_en: Use 'a' before a singular countable noun.

wrong: He hurt him while playing.
correct: He hurt himself while playing.
explanation_hi: जब subject और object एक ही व्यक्ति हो तो reflexive pronoun आता है।
explanation_en: Use reflexive pronoun when the subject and object refer to the same person.

wrong: Please help yourself with the food.
correct: Please help yourself with the food.
explanation_hi: 'Help yourself' सही reflexive expression है।
explanation_en: 'Help yourself' is the correct reflexive expression; this sentence is correct.

wrong: The man which came here is my uncle.
correct: The man who came here is my uncle.
explanation_hi: व्यक्तियों के लिए 'which' की जगह 'who' का प्रयोग होता है।
explanation_en: Use 'who' (not 'which') for persons.

wrong: The book which I borrowed it is good.
correct: The book which I borrowed is good.
explanation_hi: Relative clause में extra pronoun नहीं आता।
explanation_en: Do not repeat the pronoun in a relative clause.

wrong: Between you and I, this is wrong.
correct: Between you and me, this is wrong.
explanation_hi: Preposition के बाद objective case (me) आता है।
explanation_en: Use objective case after prepositions; 'between you and me'.

wrong: Its my book.
correct: It's my book.
explanation_hi: 'Its' possessive है; 'It's' = It is। यहाँ 'It is' के लिए 'It's' सही है।
explanation_en: 'Its' is possessive; 'It's' is a contraction of 'it is'.

wrong: The team played their best.
correct: The team played its best.
explanation_hi: Collective noun एक unit के रूप में singular pronoun लेता है।
explanation_en: When a collective noun acts as a unit, use singular pronoun 'its'.

wrong: Each student must bring their own pen.
correct: Each student must bring his or her own pen.
explanation_hi: Traditional grammar में 'each' के साथ singular pronoun आता है।
explanation_en: In formal/exam usage, 'each' takes singular pronoun 'his or her'.

wrong: Everyone should do their work honestly.
correct: Everyone should do his or her work honestly.
explanation_hi: Formal grammar में indefinite pronouns singular pronoun लेते हैं।
explanation_en: In formal grammar, indefinite pronouns take singular pronoun.

wrong: This is the boy who's bag was stolen.
correct: This is the boy whose bag was stolen.
explanation_hi: 'Whose' possessive relative pronoun है; 'who's' = who is।
explanation_en: 'Whose' is a possessive relative pronoun; 'who's' means 'who is'.

wrong: Him and his friend went to Delhi.
correct: He and his friend went to Delhi.
explanation_hi: Subject position में nominative case (He) आता है।
explanation_en: Use nominative case (He/She/They) for subjects.

wrong: The teacher scolded he.
correct: The teacher scolded him.
explanation_hi: Object position में objective case (him) आता है।
explanation_en: Use objective case (him/her/them) for objects.

wrong: It was me who called you.
correct: It was I who called you.
explanation_hi: Formal English में 'It is I' grammatically correct है।
explanation_en: In formal grammar, 'It is I' is correct (nominative case after 'be').

wrong: She is as tall as him.
correct: She is as tall as he (is).
explanation_hi: 'As...as' comparison में nominative case प्रयोग होता है।
explanation_en: Use nominative case in comparisons with 'as...as'.

wrong: You should to attend the class.
correct: You should attend the class.
explanation_hi: Modal verbs के बाद bare infinitive आता है; 'to' नहीं लगता।
explanation_en: Use bare infinitive after modal verbs; do not add 'to'.

wrong: He might to come tomorrow.
correct: He might come tomorrow.
explanation_hi: Modal verb 'might' के बाद bare infinitive आता है।
explanation_en: Use bare infinitive after modal 'might'.

wrong: She would to help you.
correct: She would help you.
explanation_hi: Modal verb के बाद bare infinitive आता है।
explanation_en: Use bare infinitive after modal 'would'.

wrong: You must to finish this today.
correct: You must finish this today.
explanation_hi: Modal 'must' के बाद bare infinitive आता है।
explanation_en: Do not use 'to' after modal 'must'.

wrong: He dares to not speak the truth.
correct: He dare not speak the truth.
explanation_hi: 'Dare' modal के रूप में 'not' के बाद bare infinitive लेता है।
explanation_en: When 'dare' is used as a modal, use 'dare not + bare infinitive'.

wrong: We shall met tomorrow.
correct: We shall meet tomorrow.
explanation_hi: Modal 'shall' के बाद verb की base form आती है।
explanation_en: Use base form after modal 'shall'.

wrong: He need not to worry.
correct: He need not worry.
explanation_hi: 'Need' modal के रूप में 'not' के बाद bare infinitive लेता है।
explanation_en: When 'need' is a modal, use 'need not + bare infinitive' without 'to'.

wrong: You ought attend the meeting.
correct: You ought to attend the meeting.
explanation_hi: 'Ought to' के साथ 'to' हमेशा आता है।
explanation_en: 'Ought' always takes 'to'; use 'ought to + infinitive'.

wrong: He may be went there.
correct: He may have gone there.
explanation_hi: Past possibility के लिए 'may have + past participle' आता है।
explanation_en: Use 'may have + past participle' for past possibility.

wrong: She would have went there.
correct: She would have gone there.
explanation_hi: Perfect modal में 'have + past participle' आता है।
explanation_en: Use 'would have + past participle' (not past tense).

wrong: He should has completed the work.
correct: He should have completed the work.
explanation_hi: 'Should have + past participle' सही structure है।
explanation_en: Use 'should have + past participle'.

wrong: I used to can swim.
correct: I used to be able to swim.
explanation_hi: Modal के past के लिए 'used to be able to' प्रयोग होता है।
explanation_en: Do not combine 'used to' with a modal; use 'used to be able to'.

wrong: He said that he is tired.
correct: He said that he was tired.
explanation_hi: Reported speech में main verb past होने पर verb का tense back-shift होता है।
explanation_en: In indirect speech, tense shifts back when the reporting verb is past.

wrong: She said, 'I will help you.'
correct: She said that she would help me.
explanation_hi: Direct speech को indirect में बदलने पर 'will' → 'would' और pronouns बदलते हैं।
explanation_en: In indirect speech, 'will' becomes 'would' and pronouns change accordingly.

wrong: He told that he was ill.
correct: He said that he was ill.
explanation_hi: 'Tell' के बाद object आना चाहिए; 'said that' सही है।
explanation_en: 'Tell' must have an object (tell someone); use 'said that' without object.

wrong: She asked me that where I lived.
correct: She asked me where I lived.
explanation_hi: Indirect question में 'that' नहीं आता।
explanation_en: Do not use 'that' to introduce an indirect question.

wrong: He asked me that what I wanted.
correct: He asked me what I wanted.
explanation_hi: Indirect question में 'that' नहीं आता; question word clause बनती है।
explanation_en: Do not use 'that' before question words in indirect speech.

wrong: She said me that she was happy.
correct: She told me that she was happy.
explanation_hi: 'Said' के साथ indirect object नहीं आता; 'told' सही है।
explanation_en: Use 'told me' (not 'said me'); 'say' does not take a direct object.

wrong: He ordered me that I should sit down.
correct: He ordered me to sit down.
explanation_hi: Order/command के liye infinitive structure प्रयोग होता है।
explanation_en: Use 'ordered someone to + infinitive' for commands in indirect speech.

wrong: The teacher said me to be quiet.
correct: The teacher told me to be quiet.
explanation_hi: 'Said' के बाद indirect object नहीं आता।
explanation_en: Use 'told me' (not 'said me') when a direct object follows.

wrong: He advised me that I should rest.
correct: He advised me to rest.
explanation_hi: Advice indirect speech में 'advised someone to + infinitive' बनती है।
explanation_en: Use 'advised someone to + infinitive' in indirect speech.

wrong: She requested him that he should help her.
correct: She requested him to help her.
explanation_hi: Request indirect speech में 'requested someone to + infinitive' बनती है।
explanation_en: Use 'requested someone to + infinitive' in indirect speech.

wrong: He said he will come tomorrow.
correct: He said he would come the next day.
explanation_hi: Past reporting में 'will' → 'would' और 'tomorrow' → 'the next day' बदलता है।
explanation_en: In past indirect speech, 'will' becomes 'would' and 'tomorrow' becomes 'the next day'.

wrong: The letter was written by him yesterday.
correct: The letter was written by him yesterday.
explanation_hi: Passive voice सही है: was + past participle + by + agent।
explanation_en: This passive construction is correct: was + past participle + by + agent.

wrong: The work is being did by him.
correct: The work is being done by him.
explanation_hi: Passive में past participle (done) आता है, not 'did'।
explanation_en: Use past participle 'done' in passive voice, not 'did'.

wrong: The letter has been wrote by her.
correct: The letter has been written by her.
explanation_hi: Perfect passive में past participle 'written' आता है।
explanation_en: Use past participle 'written' in perfect passive construction.

wrong: He was given a prize by the teacher.
correct: He was given a prize by the teacher.
explanation_hi: यह सही passive construction है।
explanation_en: This is correct passive construction with indirect object as subject.

wrong: The thief was catched by the police.
correct: The thief was caught by the police.
explanation_hi: 'Catch' का past participle 'caught' है।
explanation_en: The past participle of 'catch' is 'caught'.

wrong: She is knowing by everyone.
correct: She is known to everyone.
explanation_hi: Stative verbs passive में नहीं आते; 'known to' सही phrase है।
explanation_en: Stative verbs like 'know' use 'known to' in passive; they do not take 'being known'.

wrong: The match is been played.
correct: The match is being played.
explanation_hi: Present continuous passive में 'is being + past participle' आता है।
explanation_en: Present continuous passive: 'is being + past participle'.

wrong: He has been gave the task.
correct: He has been given the task.
explanation_hi: Perfect passive में 'been + past participle' आता है।
explanation_en: Use 'been + past participle'; 'given' not 'gave'.

wrong: If he will study hard, he will pass.
correct: If he studies hard, he will pass.
explanation_hi: Type 1 conditional में 'if clause' में simple present आता है।
explanation_en: In Type 1 conditional, use simple present in the 'if-clause', not 'will'.

wrong: If I would know the answer, I would tell you.
correct: If I knew the answer, I would tell you.
explanation_hi: Type 2 conditional में 'if clause' में simple past आता है।
explanation_en: In Type 2 conditional, use simple past in the 'if-clause', not 'would'.

wrong: If he had studied, he will have passed.
correct: If he had studied, he would have passed.
explanation_hi: Type 3 conditional में 'would have + past participle' आता है।
explanation_en: In Type 3 conditional, use 'would have + past participle' in the main clause.

wrong: If you heat ice, it will melt.
correct: If you heat ice, it melts.
explanation_hi: Type 0 conditional (general truth) में दोनों clauses simple present होती हैं।
explanation_en: In Type 0 conditional (universal truth), both clauses use simple present.

wrong: Unless you will not study, you will fail.
correct: Unless you study, you will fail.
explanation_hi: 'Unless' में negation पहले से होता है; 'not' जोड़ना गलत है।
explanation_en: 'Unless' already contains a negative meaning; do not add 'not'.

wrong: Provided that he will agree, we can proceed.
correct: Provided that he agrees, we can proceed.
explanation_hi: 'Provided that' conditional clause में simple present आता है।
explanation_en: Use simple present (not 'will') after 'provided that'.

wrong: In case he will come, inform me.
correct: In case he comes, inform me.
explanation_hi: 'In case' के बाद simple present आता है।
explanation_en: Use simple present after 'in case', not 'will'.

wrong: Neither he nor his friends is coming.
correct: Neither he nor his friends are coming.
explanation_hi: Verb nearest subject (friends-plural) के अनुसार आता है।
explanation_en: With 'neither...nor', verb agrees with the nearest subject.

wrong: Not only he plays cricket but also he paints.
correct: Not only does he play cricket but he also paints.
explanation_hi: 'Not only' sentence शुरू में आने पर inversion होता है।
explanation_en: When 'not only' begins a sentence, use auxiliary inversion.

wrong: Both he as well as his friend are wrong.
correct: Both he and his friend are wrong.
explanation_hi: 'Both' के साथ 'and' आता है, 'as well as' नहीं।
explanation_en: 'Both' is always paired with 'and', not 'as well as'.

wrong: Either he or you is responsible.
correct: Either he or you are responsible.
explanation_hi: Verb nearest subject (you-plural) के अनुसार आता है।
explanation_en: With 'either...or', the verb agrees with the nearest subject.

wrong: Although he was tired, but he continued.
correct: Although he was tired, he continued.
explanation_hi: 'Although' और 'but' एक साथ नहीं आते।
explanation_en: Do not use 'but' with 'although'; they are both connectors for contrast.

wrong: Though she studied hard, yet she failed.
correct: Though she studied hard, she failed.
explanation_hi: 'Though' के साथ 'yet' आवश्यक नहीं है; दोनों एक साथ नहीं आते।
explanation_en: Do not use 'yet' with 'though'; they serve the same purpose.

wrong: Since he was ill therefore he could not come.
correct: Since he was ill, he could not come.
explanation_hi: 'Since' और 'therefore' एक साथ नहीं आते।
explanation_en: Do not use 'therefore' with 'since'; they serve the same causal purpose.

wrong: He is so brave that he cannot be frightened.
correct: He is so brave that he can be frightened by nothing.
explanation_hi: 'So brave that he cannot' meaning को check करें; 'too brave to be frightened' अधिक natural है।
explanation_en: Check meaning carefully with 'so...that' constructions involving negatives.

wrong: Scarcely he had left when it began to rain.
correct: Scarcely had he left when it began to rain.
explanation_hi: 'Scarcely' sentence शुरू में आने पर inversion होता है।
explanation_en: Use auxiliary inversion when 'scarcely' begins a sentence.

wrong: Barely he finished when the bell rang.
correct: Barely had he finished when the bell rang.
explanation_hi: 'Barely' sentence शुरू में आने पर inversion होता है।
explanation_en: Use auxiliary inversion when 'barely' begins a sentence.

wrong: He is too weak that he cannot walk.
correct: He is too weak to walk.
explanation_hi: 'Too...to' structure में 'that' नहीं आता।
explanation_en: Use 'too + adjective + to + infinitive', not 'too...that'.

wrong: He works not only sincerely but also he is honest.
correct: He is not only sincere but also honest.
explanation_hi: 'Not only...but also' parallel structure में होना चाहिए।
explanation_en: 'Not only...but also' must connect grammatically parallel elements.

wrong: This is a new innovation.
correct: This is an innovation.
explanation_hi: 'Innovation' में new का अर्थ पहले से होता है।
explanation_en: 'Innovation' already means something new; 'new' is redundant.

wrong: He gave a free gift to her.
correct: He gave a gift to her.
explanation_hi: 'Gift' में free का अर्थ पहले से होता है।
explanation_en: A gift is by definition free; 'free' is redundant.

wrong: The past history shows this is wrong.
correct: History shows this is wrong.
explanation_hi: 'History' में past का अर्थ पहले से होता है।
explanation_en: 'History' already refers to the past; 'past' is redundant.

wrong: He joined together with them.
correct: He joined them.
explanation_hi: 'Join' में together का अर्थ पहले से होता है।
explanation_en: 'Join' already implies coming together; 'together' is redundant.

wrong: Please forward it on ahead.
correct: Please forward it.
explanation_hi: 'Forward' में ahead का अर्थ पहले से होता है।
explanation_en: 'Forward' already means to send ahead; 'on ahead' is redundant.

wrong: He finally ended up at last.
correct: He finally ended up.
explanation_hi: 'Finally' और 'at last' दोनों एक ही अर्थ देते हैं।
explanation_en: 'Finally' and 'at last' are redundant together.

wrong: She is an ATM machine.
correct: She withdrew money from an ATM.
explanation_hi: 'ATM' में 'Machine' का अर्थ पहले से होता है।
explanation_en: 'ATM' stands for Automated Teller Machine; 'machine' is redundant.

wrong: Please enter your PIN number.
correct: Please enter your PIN.
explanation_hi: 'PIN' में 'Number' का अर्थ पहले से होता है।
explanation_en: 'PIN' stands for Personal Identification Number; 'number' is redundant.

wrong: He made an unexpected surprise visit.
correct: He made a surprise visit.
explanation_hi: 'Surprise' में unexpected का अर्थ पहले से होता है।
explanation_en: A surprise is by definition unexpected; 'unexpected' is redundant.

wrong: The two twins look alike.
correct: The twins look alike.
explanation_hi: 'Twins' में two का अर्थ पहले से होता है।
explanation_en: 'Twins' already means two; 'two' is redundant.

wrong: He wrote his autobiography of his own life.
correct: He wrote his autobiography.
explanation_hi: 'Autobiography' में 'of his own life' का अर्थ पहले से होता है।
explanation_en: 'Autobiography' already means the story of one's own life.

wrong: She is a widow woman.
correct: She is a widow.
explanation_hi: 'Widow' में woman का अर्थ पहले से होता है।
explanation_en: 'Widow' is always female; 'woman' is redundant.

wrong: He is a temporary stopgap measure.
correct: It is a stopgap measure.
explanation_hi: 'Stopgap' में temporary का अर्थ पहले से होता है।
explanation_en: A stopgap is by definition temporary; the word is redundant.

wrong: Please reduce down the volume.
correct: Please reduce the volume.
explanation_hi: 'Reduce' में down का अर्थ पहले से होता है।
explanation_en: 'Reduce' already means to bring down; 'down' is redundant.

wrong: Walking down the street, the trees looked beautiful.
correct: Walking down the street, I noticed the trees looked beautiful.
explanation_hi: Participial phrase का subject main clause के subject से मेल खाना चाहिए।
explanation_en: The participial phrase must relate to the subject of the main clause.

wrong: Having finished the work, the TV was switched on.
correct: Having finished the work, he switched on the TV.
explanation_hi: Dangling participle: participial phrase का subject missing है।
explanation_en: Dangling participle error; the doer of 'having finished' must be the sentence subject.

wrong: Being a hot day, we decided to stay indoors.
correct: As it was a hot day, we decided to stay indoors.
explanation_hi: Dangling participle: 'Being a hot day' का कोई subject नहीं है।
explanation_en: Dangling modifier; rewrite to avoid the participial phrase.

wrong: He only eats vegetables.
correct: He eats only vegetables.
explanation_hi: 'Only' को उस शब्द के पास रखना चाहिए जिसे वह modify करे।
explanation_en: Place 'only' immediately before the word it modifies.

wrong: She almost drove her children to school every day.
correct: She drove her children to school almost every day.
explanation_hi: 'Almost' को 'every day' के पास रखना चाहिए।
explanation_en: Place 'almost' next to the word it modifies.

wrong: Running quickly, the bus was caught.
correct: Running quickly, he caught the bus.
explanation_hi: Participial phrase का subject main clause के subject से मिलना चाहिए।
explanation_en: The subject of the participial phrase must match the subject of the main clause.

wrong: To improve your writing, books should be read.
correct: To improve your writing, you should read books.
explanation_hi: Infinitive phrase का implied subject main clause के subject से मिलना चाहिए।
explanation_en: The implied subject of the infinitive must match the main clause subject.

wrong: She likes singing, dancing and to read.
correct: She likes singing, dancing and reading.
explanation_hi: Parallel structure में सभी elements एक ही form में होने चाहिए।
explanation_en: Maintain parallel structure; all items should be in the same grammatical form.

wrong: He is tall, dark and has intelligence.
correct: He is tall, dark and intelligent.
explanation_hi: Coordinate adjectives parallel होने चाहिए।
explanation_en: Parallel structure requires all adjectives; use 'intelligent' not 'has intelligence'.

wrong: She not only sings but also dancing.
correct: She not only sings but also dances.
explanation_hi: 'Not only...but also' parallel structure के लिए दोनों parts same form में होने चाहिए।
explanation_en: Maintain parallel form with 'not only...but also'.

wrong: He prefers reading to watch TV.
correct: He prefers reading to watching TV.
explanation_hi: 'Prefer gerund to gerund' — दोनों gerund होने चाहिए।
explanation_en: Both elements after 'prefer...to' should be in the same form (gerund).

wrong: To err is human, forgiving is divine.
correct: To err is human; to forgive is divine.
explanation_hi: Parallel structure — दोनों elements infinitive होने चाहिए।
explanation_en: Parallel structure requires matching forms; both should be infinitives.

wrong: He works quickly, accurately, and in a careful way.
correct: He works quickly, accurately and carefully.
explanation_hi: Parallel adverbs एक ही form में होने चाहिए।
explanation_en: Use parallel adverb forms; 'carefully' not 'in a careful way'.

wrong: He is a doctor, isn't it?
correct: He is a doctor, isn't he?
explanation_hi: Question tag में subject pronoun main clause के subject से मेल खाना चाहिए।
explanation_en: The tag pronoun must match the subject of the main clause.

wrong: She doesn't like coffee, does it?
correct: She doesn't like coffee, does she?
explanation_hi: Tag question में pronoun 'she' होना चाहिए।
explanation_en: Use correct pronoun in question tag.

wrong: Let us go, isn't it?
correct: Let us go, shall we?
explanation_hi: 'Let us' के साथ 'shall we?' question tag आता है।
explanation_en: Use 'shall we?' as the tag for 'let us' suggestions.

wrong: He can swim, can't it?
correct: He can swim, can't he?
explanation_hi: Tag में subject pronoun मिलना चाहिए।
explanation_en: The question tag must use the matching subject pronoun.

wrong: Nobody came, did they?
correct: Nobody came, did they?
explanation_hi: Negative indefinite pronouns (nobody, no one) के साथ plural tag 'they' आता है।
explanation_en: With negative indefinites like 'nobody', use plural pronoun 'they' in the tag.

wrong: She has finished, hasn't she?
correct: She has finished, hasn't she?
explanation_hi: यह सही question tag है।
explanation_en: This is the correct question tag.

wrong: I am right, am I not?
correct: I am right, aren't I?
explanation_hi: 'Am I not?' formal है; 'Aren't I?' अधिक प्रचलित है।
explanation_en: 'Aren't I?' is the standard question tag for 'I am'.

wrong: He used to play cricket, used he not?
correct: He used to play cricket, didn't he?
explanation_hi: 'Used to' के साथ 'didn't he?' question tag आता है।
explanation_en: Use 'didn't he?' as the question tag for 'used to'.

wrong: The house which roof is red is mine.
correct: The house whose roof is red is mine.
explanation_hi: Possession के लिए 'whose' relative pronoun आता है।
explanation_en: Use 'whose' for possession in relative clauses.

wrong: This is the place where I was born in.
correct: This is the place where I was born.
explanation_hi: 'Where' के बाद preposition अनावश्यक है।
explanation_en: Do not add 'in' after 'where' in a relative clause.

wrong: He is a man which everyone trusts.
correct: He is a man whom everyone trusts.
explanation_hi: Object position में person के लिए 'whom' आता है।
explanation_en: Use 'whom' (not 'which') when referring to a person in object position.

wrong: The reason why he failed is that he was careless.
correct: The reason he failed is that he was careless.
explanation_hi: 'Reason why' में 'why' अनावश्यक है।
explanation_en: 'The reason' alone is sufficient; 'why' is redundant.

wrong: She is the one which I trust the most.
correct: She is the one whom I trust the most.
explanation_hi: Person के लिए 'whom' आता है जब object position में हो।
explanation_en: Use 'whom' for persons in object position.

wrong: I know the man who you met him.
correct: I know the man whom you met.
explanation_hi: Relative clause में extra pronoun नहीं आता।
explanation_en: Do not repeat the pronoun (him) in a relative clause.

wrong: She sings very beautiful.
correct: She sings very beautifully.
explanation_hi: Verb को modify करने के लिए adverb आता है, adjective नहीं।
explanation_en: Use adverb 'beautifully' to modify the verb 'sings'.

wrong: He spoke very polite.
correct: He spoke very politely.
explanation_hi: Verb modify करने के लिए adverb (politely) आता है।
explanation_en: Use adverb form to modify a verb.

wrong: She is a good cook but cooks bad.
correct: She is a good cook but cooks badly.
explanation_hi: Verb modify करने के लिए adverb 'badly' आता है।
explanation_en: Use adverb 'badly' to modify the verb 'cooks'.

wrong: He drives the car careless.
correct: He drives the car carelessly.
explanation_hi: Verb modify करने के लिए adverb (-ly form) आता है।
explanation_en: Use adverb form 'carelessly' to modify the verb.

wrong: I feel badly about the incident.
correct: I feel bad about the incident.
explanation_hi: Linking verb के बाद adjective आता है, adverb नहीं।
explanation_en: Use adjective 'bad' after the linking verb 'feel'.

wrong: She looks beautifully.
correct: She looks beautiful.
explanation_hi: Linking verb 'looks' के बाद adjective आता है।
explanation_en: Use adjective 'beautiful' after the linking verb 'looks'.

wrong: He is the most cleverest student.
correct: He is the cleverest student.
explanation_hi: Double superlative गलत है।
explanation_en: Do not use double superlative.

wrong: The younger of the three sisters is Meera.
correct: The youngest of the three sisters is Meera.
explanation_hi: तीन या अधिक के लिए superlative degree प्रयोग होती है।
explanation_en: Use superlative (not comparative) when referring to three or more.

wrong: She writes as good as him.
correct: She writes as well as he does.
explanation_hi: Verb modify करने के लिए adverb 'well' आता है।
explanation_en: Use adverb 'well' (not adjective 'good') to modify the verb 'writes'.

wrong: I have seen him yesterday.
correct: I saw him yesterday.
explanation_hi: Definite past time ('yesterday') के साथ simple past आता है।
explanation_en: Use simple past with definite past time expressions like 'yesterday'.

wrong: She has completed the work two days ago.
correct: She completed the work two days ago.
explanation_hi: Definite past ('two days ago') के साथ simple past आता है।
explanation_en: Use simple past with 'ago'; do not use present perfect.

wrong: When I will reach home, I will call you.
correct: When I reach home, I will call you.
explanation_hi: Time clause में simple present आता है; 'will' नहीं।
explanation_en: Use simple present in time clauses beginning with 'when', 'after', 'before', 'until'.

wrong: After he will finish, he will leave.
correct: After he finishes, he will leave.
explanation_hi: Time clause में simple present आता है।
explanation_en: Use simple present in time clauses with 'after'.

wrong: He was sleeping when I will arrive.
correct: He was sleeping when I arrived.
explanation_hi: Past time के लिए simple past; 'will' future tense है।
explanation_en: Use past tense consistently; 'will arrive' is incorrect here.

wrong: By the time she arrives, I will finish the work.
correct: By the time she arrives, I will have finished the work.
explanation_hi: 'By the time' के साथ future perfect आता है।
explanation_en: Use future perfect ('will have finished') with 'by the time'.

wrong: She is working here since 2010.
correct: She has been working here since 2010.
explanation_hi: 'Since' के साथ present perfect continuous tense आता है।
explanation_en: Use present perfect continuous tense with 'since'.

wrong: He knows her since childhood.
correct: He has known her since childhood.
explanation_hi: 'Since' के साथ perfect tense आता है।
explanation_en: Use present perfect tense with 'since'.

wrong: The effect of pollution affects the health badly.
correct: The effects of pollution affect health badly.
explanation_hi: 'Effect' noun है; 'affect' verb है। इनका प्रयोग भिन्न है।
explanation_en: 'Effect' is a noun; 'affect' is a verb. Do not confuse them.

wrong: He rose the flag.
correct: He raised the flag.
explanation_hi: 'Raise' transitive verb है (object लेता है); 'rise' intransitive है।
explanation_en: 'Raise' is transitive (takes object); 'rise' is intransitive.

wrong: The sun rises the horizon.
correct: The sun rises above the horizon.
explanation_hi: 'Rise' intransitive verb है; object directly नहीं लेता।
explanation_en: 'Rise' is intransitive and does not take a direct object.

wrong: He laid on the bed all day.
correct: He lay on the bed all day.
explanation_hi: 'Lie' (लेटना) past tense 'lay' है; 'laid' 'lay' (रखना) का past है।
explanation_en: 'Lay' is the past tense of 'lie' (recline); 'laid' is past of 'lay' (place).

wrong: She lied the books on the table.
correct: She laid the books on the table.
explanation_hi: 'Lay' (रखना) का past tense 'laid' है।
explanation_en: Past tense of 'lay' (to place) is 'laid'.

wrong: I shall borrow you my pen.
correct: I shall lend you my pen.
explanation_hi: 'Lend' = उधार देना; 'borrow' = उधार लेना।
explanation_en: 'Lend' means to give temporarily; 'borrow' means to take temporarily.

wrong: He has less books than her.
correct: He has fewer books than her.
explanation_hi: Countable noun के साथ 'fewer' आता है।
explanation_en: Use 'fewer' with countable nouns; 'less' is for uncountable.

wrong: He is elder than his brother.
correct: He is older than his brother.
explanation_hi: 'Elder' family relation के लिए है और 'than' के साथ नहीं आता; 'older' तुलना के लिए है।
explanation_en: 'Elder' is used for family relations and cannot take 'than'; use 'older' for comparison.

wrong: She is the eldest of the two sisters.
correct: She is the elder of the two sisters.
explanation_hi: दो के लिए comparative (elder) प्रयोग होता है।
explanation_en: Use comparative form for two; 'elder' for family, 'older' for general.

wrong: Bring these books to me when you will come.
correct: Bring these books to me when you come.
explanation_hi: Time clause में simple present आता है।
explanation_en: Use simple present in time clauses.
